AccountDeleteRequest.description:
Confirmation for an irreversible deletion.

`currentPassword` is optional in the schema and required in practice for any
account that has one -- an OAuth-only account has no password to check, and
a schema-level `required` would make the request impossible to satisfy for
those users. The server decides; see `IdentityService.delete_account`.

`confirm` must be the literal string `DELETE`. It is not security -- anyone
who can send the password can send the word -- it is there so that a
mis-wired client cannot delete an account by calling the wrong endpoint with
an empty body.
AccountDeleteRequest.title: AccountDeleteRequest

ProfileUpdateRequest.description:
A PATCH: omit a field to leave it alone. `null` is not a way to clear one.

Both fields were nullable and both crashed the endpoint with a 500 —
`{"name": null}` violated the column's NOT NULL on commit, and
`{"settings": null}` made the service iterate a `None`. Any authenticated
caller could do it, and the contract said both were acceptable.

Rejecting an explicit null turns those into the 422 the contract already
declares. Nothing is lost: neither field has a meaningful empty state — you
cannot have no name, and "no settings" is not a setting. `exclude_unset` in
the handler is what still distinguishes "not supplied" from "supplied", so
omission continues to mean "leave it alone".

Found by `tests/integration/test_contract_conformance.py`, which generates
exactly this kind of payload and is why property-based testing earns its
place next to hand-written cases.
ProfileUpdateRequest.title: ProfileUpdateRequest

info.description:
Real-time scam detection for audio and text.

Authenticate with a user access token or an API key; both are sent as `Authorization: Bearer <value>` and are distinguished by the `go3_` key prefix.

Errors share one envelope -- branch on `error.code`, never on `error.message`. Every response carries `X-Request-Id`; quote it in bug reports.

**Live session channels** (`/v1/sessions/{session_id}/audio` and `/v1/sessions/{session_id}/stream`) use WebSocket, not HTTP. They are not listed under `paths` because OpenAPI 3.x has no first-class WebSocket support; their frame shapes and close codes are declared in the `x-websockets` extension at the top level of this document.
info.title: GuardianO3 API

get.description: Sessions, analyses, verdicts and audio minutes for a rolling window. Organization-wide for organization members; your own otherwise. `environment=live` counts live API keys; `environment=test` counts test keys and the console sandbox. The two are never combined. Requires a signed-in user; API keys are not accepted.

post.description:
Requires the `analysis:write` scope. Uploads are capped at `ANALYZE_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` and must carry an audio content type. Clips longer than `ANALYZE_MAX_AUDIO_SECONDS` (120 s by default) are refused with `413`, not truncated -- send the part of the audio to be scored, or stream live audio over the session WebSockets in real time. WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, MP4/M4A and WebM are decoded and resampled server-side; a file that cannot be decoded is refused with `415`. If transcription fails the response is `502` (or `504` on a timeout) -- never a low-risk verdict on audio that was not heard.

`Idempotency-Key` is **not** supported here: fingerprinting the payload would mean holding and hashing the whole upload a second time, which doubles the memory cost of the largest request the API accepts. Retry safety for audio comes from the request being stateless -- the audio is not persisted, so a duplicate costs a re-analysis (and counts as a second analysis in analytics), not a duplicate record of the audio.

x-websockets.description:
Binary uplink. Send raw PCM audio (16-bit signed, 16 kHz, mono) after authenticating.

1. Send the `AuthFrame` as the first text frame. A user access token or an API key carrying `sessions:write`.
2. Wait for `ReadyFrame`.
3. Send binary PCM frames. Audio is analysed in chunks of about 4 s (128 KB); a `LaggingFrame` means audio is arriving faster than it can be processed and a chunk was dropped.

Decisions do not come back on this channel -- open the `/stream` channel for the same session. An `ErrorFrame` precedes any close the server initiates.

clientToServer.description: Raw PCM audio, 16-bit signed little-endian, 16 kHz, mono.

x-websockets.description:
Text downlink. Connect after `POST /v1/sessions`; every frame is JSON and carries a `type`.

1. Send the `AuthFrame` as the first text frame. A user access token or an API key carrying `sessions:read`.
2. Wait for `ReadyFrame`.
3. Handle frames by `type`. Ignore types you do not recognise -- new ones may be added without a version change.

**Provisional decisions.** A `DecisionFrame` with `verificationStatus: pending` is provisional: a `DecisionUpdateFrame` for the *same* chunk follows. Replace the earlier decision in place; do not append. The update's values, including `riskLevel`, supersede the provisional ones.

`PingFrame` arrives after 20 s of silence and needs no reply. An `ErrorFrame` precedes any close the server initiates.

**Unheard audio.** A `DegradedFrame` means a stretch of the audio could not be transcribed, so no decision covers it; the session goes on. Do not read a quiet stream as "nothing suspicious" while these arrive.
